subject: MSA Annex: network isolation matrix & legal redline timeline
messages:
From: Sandra Halpert <sandra.halpert@medtech.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@medtech.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Network isolation specifics for Private deployment

Laura —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We like Redwood's approach but our security team needs more granular commitments in the MSA Annex about network zoning and operator responsibilities before we can brief procurement. Specifically:

- A simple matrix that maps which subnets/ports the on-prem operator can access vs. what remains customer-only.
- Confirmation on whether your operator (or a Redwood-managed process) can SSH into hosts for emergency fixes, and if so under what audit conditions.
- An approach for scheduled audit windows and what evidence is available (console logs, snapshot manifests).

I've attached a rough matrix from our DevOps team (20270312_MedTech_network_matrix.xlsx). Can you share a proposed redline and a timeline? Also looping in contracts (cc: Blake) for legal input.

—Sandra
CISO, MedTech Inc
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Halpert <sandra.halpert@medtech.com>
Cc: Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@medtech.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network isolation specifics for Private deployment

Sandra —

Appreciate the clarity and the matrix. High level response below; Grace (legal) and Aditya (AE) are looped to coordinate redlines and the commercial timeline.

Quick answers:
- We can limit operator access to a narrowly scoped jump host and restrict all maintenance to a time-boxed maintenance window.
- SSH access by our ops will be strictly ephemeral and fully logged; we'll provide a daily access manifest and session recordings for audit windows.
- For sharing evidence we can provide signed snapshot manifests and time-stamped console traces; persistent secrets remain customer-managed.

Action items we will deliver by Tuesday: a marked-up MSA annex (redline_MSA_annex_v1.docx) and an operator-access matrix aligned with your spreadsheet. If those look good we can propose a contractual phrasing for the audit windows and escalation path.

Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Halpert <sandra.halpert@medtech.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network isolation specifics for Private deployment

Sandra — quick commercial note: if the customer requires operator SSH with session recordings and daily manifests, that will fall under our Dedicated/on-prem support SOW add-on. We can absorb minor operational access as part of the standard Order Form for the PoC, but persistent obligations for multi-year audit evidence typically map to a service addendum.

I'll draft a short SOW bullet around audit evidence frequency and corresponding fees and share by EOD. If procurement needs an internal cost projection before legal approves, say so and I'll prioritize.

Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Blake Ruiz <contracts@blakeruiz.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Halpert <sandra.halpert@medtech.com>, Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@medtech.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:44:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redline and recommended language for annex — please review

Blake / Laura / Aditya —

Attached is our proposed marked-up annex (redline_MSA_annex_v1.docx). Summary of the substantive changes and the rationale:

1) Operator access scope — we narrowed the scope to a single bastion host with time-limited ephemeral keys; access requires documented justification and two-step approval during non-emergency windows.
2) Emergency access — allowed only with customer-designated emergency contacts and with mandatory post-event forensic reports within 48 hours.
3) Audit evidence — we propose a contractual deliverable of: a) daily access manifest (CSV), b) weekly signed snapshot manifest (SHA256), c) on-request six-month console trace bundles. We exclude source code or customer data exfiltration.
4) Liability & indemnity tweaks — clarified that operator acts as a contractor with specific limitations; we pushed back on language that would permit unlimited third-party escrow or code escrow without commercial terms.

Open items for negotiation:
- Whether session recordings are retained by Redwood for more than 30 days (MedTech requested longer retention).
- Whether the customer requires a 3rd-party custody/escrow arrangement for operator keys.

Suggested next steps:
- Blake: please confirm if the liability carveouts below are acceptable or if counsel wants to counter.
- Laura / Aditya: align commercial wording on the SOW for audit evidence frequency and fees.

I'll be available for a 30-min sync with MedTech counsel tomorrow at 10am PT if that helps expedite.

—Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Halpert <sandra.halpert@medtech.com>, Blake Ruiz <contracts@blakeruiz.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@medtech.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA Annex: network isolation matrix & legal redline timeline

Sandra / Blake —

Thanks — sending the redline and the proposed operator-access matrix attached. Two asks to keep momentum:

1) Can MedTech confirm whether 90-day session retention is a hard requirement or a negotiable preference? If it's a hard requirement we'll need to add the corresponding SOW line and note the operational cost.
2) If counsel needs a neutral escrow option for keys, please outline the expected steward role (e.g., auditor-only access vs. ability to hand back keys). We can share a list of 3rd-party custodians we regularly work with.

If both answers are reasonably scoped we can aim for a redlines resolution by EOD Wednesday and present a final Order Form addendum for signatures next week.

Attachments: redline_MSA_annex_v1.docx; 20270312_MedTech_network_matrix.xlsx

Cheers,
Laura
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
